sections.heading: What Happens If You Just Pay an El Paso Speeding Ticket
paragraphs: Most people treat a speeding ticket like a parking fine — mail in the money and move on. In Texas that payment is a plea of guilty or no contest, and the court reports the conviction to the Department of Public Safety. The violation then sits on your driving record for three years, where every insurance renewal can see it. One speeding conviction commonly raises El Paso auto premiums by 20–30% for several years, which means the "cheap" $200 ticket can quietly cost $1,000 or more.

Convictions also stack. Texas suspends licenses for drivers who collect four moving-violation convictions in 12 months or seven in 24 months, and commercial drivers face even tighter limits. If you were cited for 25 mph or more over the limit, or for speeding in a school zone, many El Paso judges will not offer defensive driving at all — which makes having a lawyer negotiate the case the only practical way to keep it off your record.

The good news: speeding is a Class C misdemeanor, the court has wide discretion, and these cases are resolved by negotiation every single day. You just need someone who knows which prosecutor, which judge and which docket to ask.

sections.heading: How Attorney Robert Navar Fights Speeding Tickets
paragraphs: When you hire us online or call 915-503-1600, we file a notice of appearance with the court the same business day. That stops the clock on your appearance date and any failure-to-appear warrant, and from that point the court communicates with our office, not you.

We then pull the citation, the officer's notes and, where it exists, the radar or lidar calibration record. Many El Paso speeding tickets have fixable problems: a wrong statute number, an unposted or improperly posted limit, a device that was not calibrated on schedule, or an officer who is no longer with the department. Each of those is leverage. We present the case to the prosecutor on the next pretrial docket and negotiate the best available result.

sections.heading: Where Your Ticket Is: El Paso Municipal Court vs. County and Area Courts
paragraphs: Who wrote the ticket decides where it's filed. El Paso Police Department citations go to El Paso Municipal Court downtown. Tickets from the Sheriff's Office, a DPS state trooper on I-10 or Loop 375, or a constable go to one of the Justice of the Peace precincts. Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint and Anthony each run their own municipal courts, and each has its own prosecutor and its own habits about deferrals.

Our flat fee covers the court your ticket is actually in: $59 for El Paso Municipal and $69 for JP and the smaller city courts. If you got more than one citation at the same stop — speeding plus no insurance, for example — each additional citation is handled at a discounted add-on rate shown on the checkout page. Not sure which court it is? Use the ticket and warrant lookup and we'll find it for you.

sections.heading: Speeding Ticket Fines, Points and Surcharges in Texas
paragraphs: A Texas speeding fine is set by the court, up to a $200 maximum for most speeds, plus state court costs that typically push the total to $150–$300 in El Paso. The old Driver Responsibility Program surcharges were repealed in 2019, but Texas still keeps the points system for license suspension purposes: two points for a moving violation, three if it involved a crash.

The real cost is insurance. A single conviction stays on your record for three years, and carriers re-rate at every renewal. Compare that with a flat $59 attorney fee that in most cases means no conviction at all, and fighting the ticket is simply the cheaper choice. It's also the only choice if you drive for work, hold a CDL, or are already close to a suspension.

sections.heading: What to Do Right Now After a Speeding Ticket
paragraphs: Check the appearance date printed on your citation — in El Paso Municipal Court it's usually 10 to 20 days out. Do not pay it, do not request defensive driving yourself (doing so can lock you into a plea), and do not miss the date. Hire us before the appearance date and we'll take it from there. If the date already passed, there may be a warrant; go to our warrant recall page and call us the same day — we can usually get it lifted within 24–48 hours.
Keep your citation, your proof of insurance and your driver's license handy for the online form. That's all we need to get started.

faqs.q: Is it worth hiring a lawyer for a speeding ticket in El Paso?
faqs.a: Yes, in nearly every case. Our fee is $59–$69 per ticket, and the most common result is a dismissal or deferred disposition with no conviction. One speeding conviction typically costs far more than that in higher insurance premiums over three years.

faqs.q: Do I have to go to court if I hire you?
faqs.a: For most speeding tickets in El Paso County, no. We appear on your behalf and handle the pretrial negotiation. You would only need to appear if the case went to trial, which is rare and something we would discuss with you first.

faqs.q: Can you get a speeding ticket dismissed?
faqs.a: Often, yes — especially when the citation has defects or the officer is unavailable. When an outright dismissal isn't available, deferred disposition achieves the same practical result: the case is dismissed after a short probation period and never becomes a conviction.

faqs.q: What if I was going 25+ mph over or in a school zone?
faqs.a: Those cases are harder because many courts won't offer defensive driving, but they are exactly where a lawyer matters most. We negotiate for deferred disposition or a reduced, non-moving charge so the high speed never reaches your record.

faqs.q: My appearance date already passed. Is it too late?
faqs.a: No, but act today. A missed date usually means a warrant and a separate failure-to-appear charge. We can file an appearance, request the warrant be recalled and reset the case — see our traffic warrant recall page.

faqs.q: Does this apply to tickets from Horizon City, Socorro or the county?
faqs.a: Yes. We handle speeding tickets in El Paso Municipal Court, all El Paso County Justice of the Peace precincts, and the Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint and Anthony municipal courts.
